cases.description: A half-migrated snapshots table only gains the columns it lacks.

steps.script: CREATE TABLE snapshots(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,repo TEXT NOT NULL,revision TEXT NOT NULL,indexed_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,metadata TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}');INSERT INTO snapshots(id,repo,revision,indexed_at) VALUES(1,'owner/repo','early','2025-12-30 00:00:00');

cases.description: A version-2 database gains the waypoint tables and a rebuilt node view without losing rows.

args: SELECT id,snapshot_id,kind,name,path,line,metadata FROM nodes ORDER BY id

cases.description: Version 1 is refused and left alone.

steps.script: CREATE TABLE evidence(value);INSERT INTO evidence VALUES('retained');PRAGMA user_version=1;

cases.description: A newer version is refused and left alone.

steps.script: CREATE TABLE evidence(value);INSERT INTO evidence VALUES('retained');PRAGMA user_version=4;

cases.description: A far-future version is refused and left alone.
A view called nodes in a version-0 file is not a legacy table.

steps.script: CREATE VIEW nodes AS SELECT 1 AS id;

cases.description: A rename that collides rolls the whole migration back, schema and data.

steps.script: CREATE TABLE nodes(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY);INSERT INTO nodes VALUES('kept');CREATE TABLE legacy_nodes(other TEXT);

cases.description: A version-2 file missing its trigger is not half upgraded.

steps.script: CREATE TABLE snapshots(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);INSERT INTO snapshots VALUES(1);PRAGMA user_version=2;
